articles.author: Rohan Mehta

p: Most first-time buyers focus on the showroom price, but your true budget is the on-road price plus insurance, fuel and service for the next few years. A simple rule is to keep the monthly instalment below a comfortable share of your take-home income, leaving room for fuel and upkeep. Decide this number before you visit any showroom, because a salesperson will always have one more trim to suggest.

body.h: Match the car to your week
p: Write down how you actually drive. If most trips are short city runs, a compact automatic will reduce stress far more than extra power will. If you spend weekends on highways with family, stability and boot space should move up your list. Test the rear seat, check visibility in tight lanes and park the car once, since those small moments will repeat every single day of ownership.

body.h: Take your time with the paperwork
p: Ask for a written price breakup, check what the insurance includes, and confirm the delivery date in writing. Inspect the car in daylight before signing the delivery note, and keep every invoice. A careful hour at this stage saves months of follow-up later, and it gives you a clear record if anything needs attention under warranty.

articles.title: Petrol, CNG or electric: which should you buy?
articles.excerpt: The right fuel depends mostly on distance. At low monthly running, the higher price of an electric car or CNG kit can take many...
articles.author: Ishita Kapoor

p: The right fuel depends mostly on distance. At low monthly running, the higher price of an electric car or CNG kit can take many years to pay back, so petrol often makes sense. As your running rises, the savings grow quickly and alternatives begin to look far more attractive. Work out your typical monthly distance honestly, using a few months of real history rather than a hopeful guess.

body.h: Think about where you will refuel
p: Electric ownership is easiest with a home charger, since you start each morning with enough range for the day. Without one, you rely on public charging, which varies by city. CNG is cheap per kilometre, yet queues and limited stations can add time, and the cylinder reduces boot space. Petrol remains the simplest option when convenience matters more than running cost.

body.h: Look at the whole ownership picture
p: Compare insurance, service schedules, resale expectations and battery warranty terms, not just fuel cost. Electric cars have fewer service items but a higher purchase price, while CNG adds some maintenance to a petrol engine. The calculator on our EMI page helps you see how each choice changes the monthly commitment once you include the higher or lower purchase price.

articles.author: Ananya Rao

p: Tyre pressure is the cheapest maintenance you can do, since it affects mileage, braking and comfort together. Check it monthly when the tyres are cold, and follow the figure on the door sticker rather than a guess at the fuel pump. Also look at coolant and washer fluid levels, and keep an eye on wiper condition before the monsoon arrives each year.

body.h: Service on time, not just on distance
p: Short city trips are harder on an engine than steady highway running, so do not stretch the service schedule simply because the odometer is low. Oil ages with time as well. Keep records of every visit, as a complete service history directly improves resale value, and buyers increasingly ask to see it before they make any kind of serious offer.

Before the rains, check tyre tread, brake response and door drains, and avoid driving through deep water, because engine damage from it is costly. In summer, service the air conditioning early and park in shade where possible to protect the cabin and battery. A little planning around the seasons keeps surprise bills away and helps your car stay reliable for many years.

ev.label: Electric Car News
ev.h1: Electric car news and EV updates
ev.intro: New launches, charging developments and honest ownership costs for electric cars in India.
ev.guide: Electric car decisions depend heavily on where you will charge and how far you drive each month. Stories here focus on range, charging speed and the true cost of running an EV, rather than on headline figures alone. If you have no home charger, pay special attention to coverage of public networks in your own city.

petrol.label: Petrol Car News
petrol.intro: Launches, price changes and mileage stories for the petrol cars most Indian families buy.
petrol.guide: Petrol remains the simplest choice for buyers who do not drive very long distances, as the purchase price is lower and refuelling is easy everywhere. These stories help you compare turbo and naturally aspirated engines, and understand how each of them behaves in traffic and on open highways.

diesel.label: Diesel Car News
diesel.intro: What is changing for diesel cars, from new variants and prices to the rules that affect them.
diesel.guide: Diesel makes the most sense if you cover high monthly distances or often travel fully loaded, because its strong low-speed torque and good highway economy can offset the higher price. Before you buy, check the rules in your city, since older diesel vehicles face restrictions in some parts of the country.

cng.label: CNG Car News
cng.intro: New CNG variants, pump network growth and real running costs for budget-conscious buyers.
cng.guide: CNG can cut your fuel bill sharply, but the savings depend on having a filling station that is convenient to reach. These stories look at factory-fitted options, the boot space you give up to the cylinder, and how much driving you need to do for the extra purchase cost to pay for itself.

hybrid.label: Hybrid Car News
hybrid.intro: Strong and mild hybrid launches, real mileage and the tax rules that change what you pay.
hybrid.guide: Hybrids shine in stop-and-go traffic, where the electric motor does more of the work and the engine rests. Coverage here explains the difference between mild and strong hybrids, what happens to boot space and how state tax rules can shift the on-road price by a noticeable amount.

launches.label: New Launches
launches.intro: Everything that is arriving in showrooms, with prices, variants and what is genuinely new.
launches.guide: A launch story is most useful when it tells you what has changed for your budget. We look at which variant to choose, what rival cars offer at the same price and whether it is sensible to wait through the first batch of deliveries or book right away.

prices.label: Price Updates
prices.intro: Price hikes, new variant pricing and what each change means for your on-road cost.
prices.guide: Price revisions tend to cluster around the new year and the start of the financial year. A small change in the ex-showroom figure also affects road tax and insurance, so these stories focus on the final amount you pay, and on whether it is better to book now or wait a little.

comparisons.label: Comparisons
comparisons.h1: Car comparisons: which should you buy?
comparisons.intro: Close rivals side by side on price, space, features and powertrains, with a clear verdict.
comparisons.guide: A good comparison starts from the trims you can actually afford rather than from the most expensive versions. Each of these stories lines up price, dimensions, features and engines, and then explains which kind of buyer should choose which car, so that you can match the verdict to your own needs.

spy.label: Spy Shots
spy.h1: Car spy shots and test sightings
spy.intro: Early sightings of cars under test, and what they may tell us about upcoming models.
spy.guide: Spy shots are fun, but they are not promises. Plans change, and a camouflaged car can differ a lot from the final version. We try to separate what can actually be seen from what is only speculation, so that you can decide whether a rumoured update is really worth delaying your purchase for.

mileage.label: Mileage And Running Costs
mileage.h1: Car mileage and running cost guides
mileage.intro: Real-world fuel economy, monthly costs and simple ways of spending less on every trip.
mileage.guide: Claimed mileage figures come from laboratory tests, so they work better for comparing cars than for predicting your own fuel bill. These stories explain what changes the number in real life, from traffic and tyre pressure to speed and load, and how to estimate what a car will really cost you to run.

safety.label: Safety
safety.intro: Crash ratings, airbags and driver assistance, explained in simple and practical language.
safety.guide: Safety equipment often changes from one trim to another, so a headline crash rating may not describe the exact car you are buying. These stories explain what the ratings measure, which features matter the most in everyday driving and how to check the specification of your chosen variant.

deals.label: Offers And Discounts
deals.h1: New car offers and discount news
deals.intro: How current deals really work, and how to tell a real saving from a clever headline.
deals.guide: A big discount figure usually combines several separate benefits, and you may qualify for only some of them. These stories explain how to read an offer, what to ask the dealer and why comparing the full on-road totals is more useful than comparing the discount amounts alone.

policy.label: Policy And Rules
policy.h1: Car policy news and new rules
policy.intro: New rules on safety, emissions and tax, and how they could change what you pay for a car.
policy.guide: Government rules can quietly change prices and availability, sometimes removing a popular fuel type from a range altogether. We explain what a new rule actually requires, when it is likely to apply and what buyers should do about it, without assuming that you follow the industry closely.

sales.label: Sales Reports
sales.h1: Car sales reports and market trends
sales.intro: Which cars and segments are selling, and what those trends can mean for you as a buyer.
sales.guide: Sales trends are useful even if you do not follow the industry. A popular car usually has better service coverage and resale value, but it may also come with longer waiting periods and smaller discounts. These reports explain what the numbers could mean for your next purchase.

faqsHome.q: How do I choose the right car on Wheelora?
faqsHome.a: Start with your monthly budget and the kind of driving you do most. Filter cars by price, body type and fuel, shortlist two or three, then compare them side by side before you book a test drive.

faqsHome.q: What is the difference between ex-showroom and on-road price?
faqsHome.a: The ex-showroom price is what the manufacturer lists before local charges. The on-road price adds road tax, registration, insurance and other fees, and it changes from one city to another.

faqsHome.q: Is the information on this site final?
faqsHome.a: This version of the site is a design prototype, so prices, offers, reviews and dealer details are demo data. Always confirm the latest information with an authorised dealer.
